scope: Inventory and applicability audit for primary, corrected, and follow-up sources that could make FGKMT Hypothesis 1(2) and Maynard Proposition 9.2 numerical. This gate fixes the target contract and successor proof obligations; it does not prove the numerical distribution package.

actual_fgkmt_parameters.working_interval: n in [y,2y), with x <= y <= x*(log x)^2 and every L_i nonnegative
actual_fgkmt_parameters.exceptional_filter: one prime B chosen from a possible exceptional conductor; gcd(q,B)=1

target_contract.proposition_9_2_dependency: The implied constants depend on theta, alpha, and the constants in Bdd1, Bdd2, and Bdd3.

requirements.name: exact-centered-target
requirements.requirement: Control the Maynard centered count against #P_L,A(x)/phi_L(q), not only psi(t;q,a)-t/phi(q).

requirements.name: modulus-coverage
requirements.requirement: Cover every q <= x^(1/3) with gcd(q,B)=1 after the affine lift to modulus |a|q.

requirements.name: log-saving
requirements.requirement: Produce the relative saving (log x)^(-100*k^2) required by Hypothesis 1(2).

requirements.name: k-uniformity-or-fixed-k-reduction
requirements.requirement: Either control all k <= (log x)^(1/5), or prove that the downstream application fixes a finite k and record the resulting cutoff.

requirements.name: common-exceptional-modulus
requirements.requirement: Choose one conductor and one prime B that work simultaneously for all endpoints, forms, and moduli in the application.

requirements.name: affine-form-lift
requirements.requirement: Prove the exact bijection from n congruent to r modulo q to primes L(n) in a residue class modulo |a|q, including a<0, gcd, and admissibility cases.

requirements.name: half-open-endpoints
requirements.requirement: Transfer cumulative estimates to the half-open interval n in [y,2y) without losing endpoint or prime-power terms.

requirements.name: psi-to-prime-count
requirements.requirement: Convert von Mangoldt weighted estimates to unweighted prime counts with an explicit prime-power and partial-summation error.

requirements.name: total-population-recentering
requirements.requirement: Replace the analytic main term by the exact total #P_L,A(x)/phi_L(q) and sum the induced q-dependent correction explicitly.

requirements.name: represented-prime-density
requirements.requirement: Give an explicit positive lower bound for #P_L,A(x) so the absolute discrepancy becomes the required relative discrepancy.

requirements.name: printed-multipliers
requirements.requirement: Make every multiplier in the average theorem and the pointwise exceptional-zero term numerical for the selected parameters.

requirements.name: common-finite-cutoff
requirements.requirement: Combine all validity ranges and error absorptions into one finite x cutoff that also satisfies Proposition 9.2.

candidate_evaluations.usable_output: Correct asymptotic proof architecture with a single exceptional prime B and the required affine-form family.
candidate_evaluations.reason: The printed proof uses hidden constants and sufficiently-large cutoffs in the character and Bombieri-Vinogradov steps.

candidate_evaluations.usable_output: Explicit mean-value bounds for moduli whose least prime divisor exceeds Q1.
candidate_evaluations.reason: The rough-modulus condition is stronger than gcd(q,B)=1 and leaves the small-prime-factor moduli untreated.

candidate_evaluations.usable_output: Effective asymptotic mean-value route after excluding small moduli.
candidate_evaluations.reason: The published 2019 corollary needs Johnston's B-3 correction, and neither source supplies a ready numerical Maynard-centered package.

candidate_evaluations.usable_output: Explicit average bounds excluding a possible exceptional modulus for bounded logarithmic exponents.
candidate_evaluations.reason: The parameter ranges A<=7 or the related bounded-A range cannot deliver the exponent 100*k^2 for the H1 target; the papers are preprints.

candidate_evaluations.usable_output: Published Theorem 1.4 allows any real A>3, gives an explicit non-exceptional-modulus average bound, and Theorem 1.2 isolates an exceptional-zero contribution pointwise.
candidate_evaluations.reason: It is the closest source, but the project must still prove the actual parameter composition and all bridges rather than quote it as H1(2).

candidate_evaluations.usable_output: Explicit pointwise psi, theta, and pi bounds for each fixed modulus with computable cutoffs.
candidate_evaluations.reason: Summing the pointwise bounds over all q<=x^(1/3) does not provide the required strong average saving, and large-modulus cutoffs grow too quickly for a direct route.

candidate_evaluations.usable_output: A sharper explicit zero-free constant R=5.60 for primitive characters with conductor q<=400000.
candidate_evaluations.reason: It can improve a finite low-conductor component but is not a global Landau-Page or Bombieri-Vinogradov package.

candidate_evaluations.usable_output: An effective all-moduli Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem with a computable constant.
candidate_evaluations.reason: The available error has only a fixed log^-2 saving up to log-log factors, far weaker than log^(-100*k^2), and the constant is not printed numerically.

candidate_evaluations.usable_output: A method that alters sieve upper and lower bounds to avoid the exceptional modulus while retaining the asymptotic sieve form with effective error terms.
candidate_evaluations.reason: This recent preprint is not a direct Hypothesis 1 or Proposition 9.2 theorem and compatibility with Maynard's multidimensional weights would require a new proof.

corrections_and_cautions.rule: Do not use the printed log^(B-2) denominator without correction; Johnston 2026 Lemma 3.4 gives log^(B-3).
least_prime_factor(q)>Q1 does not mean gcd(q,B)=1 and cannot be substituted silently.
A theorem with explicit formulas is not yet the exact Maynard-centered inequality; every affine, centering, density, and cutoff bridge remains a proof obligation.
Treat as a recent unverified redesign candidate and do not promote it to the theorem input without independent source and compatibility review.

affine_recentering_identity.statement: For L(n)=a*n+b and an eligible residue r modulo q, the L-values form one residue class modulo |a|q. If M is the analytic main count at modulus |a|, then |C_q-C_1/phi_L(q)| is at most |C_q-M/phi(|a|q)| plus [phi(|a|)/phi(|a|q)]*|C_1-M/phi(|a|)|.
